applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain has an extensive network of bilateral investment treaties; applicability depends on the investor's state of nationality and treaty validity.
Convention between Spain and China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and Prevention of Fiscal Evasion, signed 1990, as amended.
Convention between Spain and the United States for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and Prevention of Fiscal Evasion, signed 1990, as amended.
Convention between Spain and the United Kingdom for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and Prevention of Fiscal Evasion, signed 2013, as amended.

Spain has a broad bilateral DTA network with European, Latin American, Asian, Middle Eastern and other jurisdictions; treaty relief requires residence, beneficial ownership and anti-abuse qualification.
European Union-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally applied in relevant parts.
European Union-United Kingdom Trade and Cooperation Agreement.

Intra-European Union bilateral investment treaties are subject to EU-law limitations, including the Achmea and Komstroy jurisprudence and the Agreement for the Termination of Bilateral Investment Treaties between EU Member States.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, particularly Articles 3, 4, 7, 8, 14, 16 and 19; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May approving the implementing regulation, particularly Articles 8 and 9; Royal Decree-Law 7/2021 of 27 April implementing EU AML amendments; and Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July establishing the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership. Beneficial ownership is generally identified by direct or indirect ownership exceeding 25 percent of capital or voting rights, or by control through other means; where no natural person is identified, senior managing officials are recorded as the fallback category.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial or companies registry of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; use consular legalization where the issuing state is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign corporate shareholder board or shareholder resolution approving the Spanish subsidiary, capital contribution, director appointment and power of attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate shareholder, authenticated by a competent notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; use consular legalization where the issuing state is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for incorporation and Spanish tax or registry filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or other legally competent authentication authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; use consular legalization where the issuing state is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Identity and address evidence for each ultimate natural-person beneficial owner and proposed director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport or national identity authority, supplemented by notarized address evidence where required
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if notarized or officially certified; ordinary passport copies generally require notarial certification where requested by the Spanish notary or obliged entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign tax-residence certificate and, where relevant, certificate of tax identification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Tax authority of the relevant country of residence or incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by an official Spanish translation where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Official Spanish sworn translation of all foreign-language corporate and ownership documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator appointed or recognized by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Spanish sworn translation; apostille or consular legalization remains applicable to the underlying foreign public document

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The Spanish obliged entity must conduct risk-based customer identification, beneficial-owner verification, purpose and business-relationship assessment, ongoing monitoring, record retention and suspicious-transaction reporting under Law 10/2010 and Royal Decree 304/2014. PEP status requires enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and enhanced ongoing monitoring. Screening must cover applicable United Nations sanctions, directly applicable European Union restrictive measures and Spanish domestic measures. OFAC screening is not generally a standalone statutory requirement in Spain but is commercially and contractually mandatory for United States nexus transactions, USD clearing, regulated counterparties and many banks. Screening must include aliases, directors, UBOs, authorized signatories, counterparties and controlling persons. Nominee arrangements do not displace UBO identification requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central online name-certification portal (https://www.rmc.es); incorporation may also be processed through the official CIRCE/PAE system where eligibility requirements are satisfied.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be sufficiently distinct from existing registered names and must include or correspond to the legal-form designation Sociedad Limitada, Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, S.L. or S.R.L. The name may be in Spanish or another permitted language, but it must be grammatically and legally acceptable to the Registro Mercantil Central. Foreign-language terms, transliterations and acronyms must not create confusion, misleading associations or prohibited official references. A foreign-language name does not eliminate the requirement to use the statutory Spanish legal-form designation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Obtain a negative name certificate from the Registro Mercantil Central before executing the incorporation deed. The certificate generally reserves the name for six months, while the certificate itself is ordinarily usable for incorporation for three months from issuance; obtain a renewed certificate if the operative period has expired. If rejected, review the stated similarity, prohibited-term or legal-form ground, select alternative names, and submit a corrected application through the RMC portal. A registrar qualification or refusal may be challenged by the applicable registry appeal to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública, generally within one month under the Reglamento del Registro Mercantil and the relevant provisions of the Mortgage Law; alternatively, judicial review may be available. The appeal should attach the refusal, the application, name-distinctiveness evidence and the proposed corrective wording. A name clearance does not authorize regulated financial, insurance, payment, telecommunications, energy or security activities.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Sociedad Limitada must have a registered office in Spain under Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the Capital Companies Act. A serviced or virtual office may be acceptable if it is a genuine address capable of receiving official communications and maintaining required corporate records, subject to the provider's authority and the notary's and registry's acceptance. For SCADA integration and substation-automation contracting, a purely virtual office creates elevated banking, tax-residence, procurement, permanent-establishment and commercial-substance risk. A physical operational location, technical personnel, equipment records and demonstrable project-management capacity are recommended where engineering, installation, commissioning or maintenance is performed in Spain.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official national percentage is published. For a newly incorporated, foreign-owned entity with a virtual office and industrial-grid activities, the estimated probability of an unannounced physical inspection or address-verification event during the first 24 months is approximately 5 percent to 15 percent; the risk may be materially higher where tax refunds, payroll, public procurement, regulated infrastructure, cash-intensive activity or inconsistent operational evidence is present. This is a compliance risk estimate, not a statutory probability.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), Articles 20-22 (incorporation), 58-59 (registered office), 62-63 (share capital), 209-210 (board of directors).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) and the corresponding Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) where the registered office is located.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (Deed of Incorporation) granted before a Spanish Notary, followed by inscription in the Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of €3,000 (approx. USD 3,300) fully subscribed and paid up in cash or in-kind at incorporation. No escrow account is required; capital must be deposited in a Spanish bank account in the company's name and evidenced by a bank certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the incorporation deed and bylaws be approved and the company be registered with the Mercantile Registry. (2) That the registered office be established at [address], Spain. (3) That the share capital of €3,000 be fully subscribed and paid as per the deed. (4) That [Name] be appointed as sole Administrator (Administrador Único) with full powers. (5) That the Administrator is authorized to execute all filings, obtain tax IDs, and open bank accounts. (6) That the company adopt the fiscal year ending December 31.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Name Non-Registration (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) – online via CIRCE or in person
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request for the proposed company name (e.g., 'SCADA Substation Automation SL') to the Central Commercial Registry. The certificate confirms no identical or confusingly similar name exists. The certificate is valid for 3 months. Provide the applicant's ID and proposed corporate purpose.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, file a new application with alternative names. If the certificate expires, reapply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Provisional Bank Account and Deposit Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any Spanish commercial bank (e.g., Banco Santander, BBVA, CaixaBank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional corporate bank account in the name of the company in formation. Deposit the minimum share capital of €3,000. Obtain a bank certificate (Certificado de Depósito) confirming the deposit and the account details. The certificate must be issued within 2 months of the deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional documentation, provide the draft deed and name certificate. If the deposit is delayed, extend the bank certificate validity by re-issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Public Deed of Incorporation (Escritura de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notary (Notario) – chosen by the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before a notary with the name certificate, bank certificate, and draft bylaws. The notary will draft and execute the deed, which includes the company name, registered office, corporate purpose (ISIC 4321 – electrical installation and SCADA integration), share capital, and appointment of the administrator. All incorporators must sign personally or via legal representative. The notary will issue the deed and a notarized copy for registration.
required_dossiers: NIE (Foreigner's Identification Number) for each incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in the bylaws or documentation, correct them and reschedule. If a non-resident lacks NIE, obtain it from the local police station or consulate before signing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for Provisional Tax ID (NIF Provisional) and Register for Taxes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – local tax office or online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days of the deed execution, file Form 036 (Censo de Empresarios) to obtain the provisional NIF (CIF) and register for corporate income tax (IS), VAT (IVA), and withholding taxes. The provisional NIF is valid for 6 months. Also register the company with the Social Security system (Seguridad Social) for employer registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, provide additional documentation as requested. If the provisional NIF expires, apply for the definitive NIF after registration in the Mercantile Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company in the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry corresponding to the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed and supporting documents to the Provincial Mercantile Registry for registration. The registry will review the deed for legal compliance. Once registered, the company acquires legal personality. The registration is published in the Official Gazette (BORME).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a defect (defecto), correct the deed or provide additional documents within the given period (usually 15 days). If the deed is rejected, re-execute before the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Definitive NIF and Finalize Corporate Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration in the Mercantile Registry, file Form 036 again to convert the provisional NIF to a definitive NIF. Also register the company for any municipal licenses (e.g., activity license) and obtain the electronic signature certificate for the company.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration from Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the definitive NIF is delayed, follow up with AEAT. If the company needs to start operations immediately, use the provisional NIF for invoicing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Consejería de Industria, Energía y Minas of the Autonomous Community (e.g., Comunidad de Madrid) – Industrial Services Directorate
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Actividad (Activity License) and, if applicable, Licencia de Apertura (Opening License) for the physical installation site

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO) – Environmental Assessment Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Categoría B) – for low-impact electrical installation and SCADA integration activities; full EIA not required unless the project involves high-voltage substations or significant land use.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Real Decreto 102/2011 (air quality) for VOC emissions from soldering or cleaning agents; wastewater discharge must meet municipal sewer limits per Real Decreto 1620/2007; waste handling per Ley 22/2011 (Residuos).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Certificado de Protección Contra Incendios) from the local fire department; structural load inspection (Inspección Técnica de Edificios) for the facility; workplace health and safety clearance (Plan de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales) per Ley 31/1995, and registration with the Social Security for occupational accident coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the AEAT electronic headquarters (Sede electrónica de la AEAT). Customs matters are administered through the AEAT Customs and Excise Department within the European Union customs framework.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains its Spanish tax identification number (NIF) by filing Form 036 with the AEAT. A provisional NIF may be obtained during incorporation and must be converted into a definitive NIF after registration with the Commercial Registry and submission of the final constitutional documents. The standard NIF format for a Spanish limited liability company begins with the legal-entity prefix B followed by seven digits and a control character. A foreign company or other non-resident legal person requiring Spanish tax registration generally applies for a NIF using Form 036, submitting its constitutional documents, evidence of legal existence, identification of directors or legal representatives, and appointment of a Spanish tax representative where legally required. Foreign documents normally require legalization or apostille and an official Spanish translation unless an applicable exemption applies. A VAT identification number (NIF-IVA) is the Spanish NIF preceded by ES and is obtained by registering in the Register of Intra-Community Operators (ROI) through Form 036. ROI registration is necessary for qualifying intra-Community supplies and acquisitions and enables inclusion in the VIES system; it is not automatically granted merely because a NIF exists. The entity must also register the relevant economic activities and tax obligations through Form 036 before commencing taxable activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Spanish SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate taxable entity and has no United States-style check-the-box election. Available statutory elections or special regimes may include Spanish tax consolidation for qualifying corporate groups, the special tax-neutral regime for qualifying restructurings, the special regime for newly created entities where statutory conditions are met, the special regime for small entities where applicable, and selected VAT elections such as the Cash Basis Special Regime, the monthly VAT refund regime, and the Intra-Community Operators Register. Hybrid mismatch rules under Spanish law implement the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive and do not provide a general elective hybrid-entity classification. A Spanish tax-resident company is generally taxed on worldwide income; a non-resident company is taxed under Non-Resident Income Tax on Spanish-source income and Spanish permanent-establishment profits.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA), supplemented for certain transactions by Spanish regional indirect taxes in the Canary Islands, Ceuta, and Melilla. Mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands apply Spanish VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold applies for Spanish VAT registration. A person carrying out an economic activity independently must register before commencing taxable activities, regardless of turnover. The obligation may arise from the first taxable transaction, importation, intra-Community acquisition, or other relevant operation. Separate registration or reporting requirements may apply for ROI, the One-Stop Shop regimes, the Immediate Supply of Information system, or non-resident VAT obligations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not currently operate a universal real-time pre-clearance system for all domestic VAT invoices. Invoices must comply with Spanish invoicing rules, including required supplier and customer identification, invoice numbering, date, description, taxable base, VAT rate, VAT amount, and applicable exemption or reverse-charge wording. Electronic invoices to Spanish public-sector entities are generally submitted through the FACe public e-invoicing infrastructure or the competent public administration platform. The Immediate Supply of Information (SII) regime requires qualifying taxpayers, including taxpayers under the monthly VAT refund regime, VAT groups, and generally taxpayers exceeding the statutory large-business threshold, to transmit invoice-register data electronically to the AEAT, normally within four calendar days subject to statutory adjustments and exclusions. Spanish computerized invoicing systems are also subject to the integrity, conservation, traceability, and anti-manipulation requirements under Royal Decree 1007/2023 and related implementing rules, including the applicable VERI*FACTU or equivalent compliance model and technical deadlines. The broader mandatory private-sector electronic invoicing regime under Law 18/2022 depends on implementing regulations and the applicable transition timetable. VAT returns and related information are generally filed electronically through the AEAT portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from mainland Spain or the Balearic Islands to a destination outside the European Union may qualify as VAT-exempt exports with the right to deduct input VAT, provided the statutory exporter or intermediary conditions are met and the export is supported by customs evidence that the goods exited the EU customs territory. The usual evidence is the electronic customs export declaration and the confirmed exit result. Intra-Community supplies of goods to a VAT-identified customer in another EU Member State may qualify for exemption with the right to deduct input VAT if the goods are transported to another Member State, the customer provides a valid EU VAT number, the supplier includes the transaction in the required recapitulative statement, and transport and commercial evidence is retained. Cross-border B2B services generally follow the place-of-supply rule and are outside the scope of Spanish VAT when the customer is established outside Spain, rather than technically being zero-rated; evidence of the customer's business status and establishment must be retained. Specific exceptions apply to services connected with real estate, passenger transport, admission to events, short-term vehicle hire, restaurants and catering, and other special categories. Export-related input VAT may be recovered through periodic VAT returns or, where applicable, the monthly refund regime, subject to ordinary deduction requirements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration submitted through the applicable EU customs system, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Electronic confirmation of exit from the EU customs territory or equivalent customs exit evidence
Commercial invoice and sales contract or purchase order identifying the goods, exporter, consignee, value, delivery terms, and destination
Transport documentation, such as bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, or courier documentation
Packing list and, where applicable, export licences, dual-use documentation, origin evidence, or sector-specific certificates
Accounting records, VAT invoice, inventory records, and reconciliation between the export declaration, invoice, transport documents, and VAT return
Evidence of customer identity and destination outside the EU, where relevant to the exemption conditions
Banking or payment evidence where useful for audit substantiation; an inward-remittance certificate is not generally a universal Spanish VAT condition for export exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain has no general foreign-exchange rule requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within 180 days. Export proceeds may generally be received through ordinary banking channels, subject to anti-money-laundering, statistical, customs, accounting, and reporting obligations. If export exemption or input VAT recovery is unsupported, the AEAT may deny the exemption or deduction, assess output VAT and statutory late-payment interest, and impose tax penalties. Penalties for incorrect VAT treatment may generally range from 50% to 150% of the improperly unpaid tax depending on the conduct, concealment, repeated infringement, and other statutory aggravating factors; voluntary late correction may instead attract statutory surcharges where applicable. False, fabricated, or deliberately manipulated customs or VAT evidence may also trigger customs sanctions, administrative penalties, seizure or forfeiture consequences, and potentially criminal tax or customs proceedings. A tax assessment may include retrospective VAT, interest, and penalties for the applicable limitation period, ordinarily four years for tax assessment rights, subject to suspension, interruption, and special statutory rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting under the Eurosystem and the European Central Bank; foreign investment and trade surveillance also touches the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones and the Ministry of Economy for FDI screening and balance-of-payments statistics (Form CE / Declaración de Inversiones Exteriores).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates within the euro area with full capital and current account convertibility; no prior exchange-control authorization is required by a non-resident shareholder to subscribe equity, receive dividends, repay shareholder loans, or repatriate liquidation proceeds of a Spanish SL. The operative frictions are fiscal rather than regulatory: dividend and interest withholding taxes (19% standard under the domestic rate, often reduced by EU or treaty provisions), transfer-pricing exit risks on the shareholder loan, and the Banco de España statistical reporting duties. Banks will nonetheless demand evidence of the Non-Resident Investor Declaration (declaración de inversión exterior) to classify inbound remittances correctly and avoid recharacterisation as unrelated proceeds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Spanish law imposes no mandatory surrender, no statutory conversion ratio, no retention period, and no repatriation deadline for export receipts. An SL may keep export proceeds in foreign currency accounts domestically or abroad, or convert them freely. The only compliance duties are statistical and fiscal: bank-facilitated transfers exceeding EUR 50,000 must be recorded in the Balance of Payments declaration (Form CE) submitted via the reporting entity; goods movements require INTRASTAT/EXTRASTAT or SAD customs filings; and the Tax Agency requires invoicing entries through the Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) digital channel.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banco Cooperativo Español, S.A. (Caja Rural Group)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. An EEA-licensed or Spanish-authorised Electronic Money Institution (EMI) may passport into Spain under PSD2 / Real Decreto-ley 19/2018 and can operate euros pre-funded wallets, IBAN accounts in the SEPA zone, and multi-currency collection for trade customers. Viable use-cases for this SCADA SL include Latin American collections, USD/EUR conversion of minor invoices, and remote payroll expenses. However, an EMI is not a substitute for the anchor treasury bank: it cannot extend credit, balances do not carry Spanish Deposit Guarantee coverage, and the Tax Agency / counterparty banks routinely require a main corporate account at an authorised credit institution for SII certification, corporate residence certificates (modelo 02), and documentary credits. The blueprint therefore rates fintech EMIs as a complementary rail with Medium feasibility and strict limitation to operating balances below EUR 500,000.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is realistically unavoidable for a newly incorporated SL with non-resident shareholders and no prior financial statements. Spanish AML law (Ley 10/2010, amended by Ley 6/2023) obliges credit institutions to verify the identity of directors and the ultimate beneficial owner; banks apply this through an in-branch or live video-identified interview of the acting managing director, plus notarial authentication of the power of attorney (poder preventivo) if any director is resident abroad. Remote opening is possible only through a minority of digital challenger banks and digital account products of tier-1 banks; these channels normally require a notary or the company's Spanish domiciliation agent to be physically present to certify the signatory. For a first-year treasury account, budget for one physical visit per director / authorised signatory and for a notarised power of attorney granted before a Spanish notary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: File created for a company incorporated less than six months prior with no audited financial statements; funds are injected only at onboarding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original escritura de constitución, Tax Agency NIF certificate, notarial certificate of the capital subscription, Registro Mercantil extract, ownership chart, and formal bank board resolution designating signatories; the signed SCADA supply or integration contract with the final utility/customer as credible business purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder domiciled in a country perceived as high-risk or non-cooperative for tax purposes, or routing through an offshore holding vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax residence certificate (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) from the shareholder's jurisdiction, corporate registry excerpt and translator certificate, a legal opinion from Spanish counsel confirming that the investment is not a conduit transaction, UBO register (Registro de Titularidades Reales) disclosure, and source-of-funds bank statements covering the capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business-purpose mismatch flagged because ISIC 4321 covers electrical installation whereas the entity will prepay suppliers of SCADA/PLC software and hardware from third countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial contract set: framework agreement, technical scope (RTU/PLC/SCADA/telemetry), geolocation of substations, bill of materials, supplier proforma invoices, Incoterms schedule, and certificates such as ISO 9001 or UNE 21427 if applicable; a one-page narrative map from contract to down payment to delivery.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large and frequent outward wire transfers to, or incoming collections from, Latin American utilities (Mexico, Colombia, Chile) under tight project settlement calendars.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full export documentation package: signed purchase orders, commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or air waybill, insurance certificate, EXTRASTAT declaration where EU goods movement is involved, and the Banco de España Form CE declaratory cover for operations above EUR 50,000; plus the master services agreement showing the buyer is a regulated electricity company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Directors hold tax residency outside Spain and do not maintain a visible physical office in Spain; corporate domiciliation is serviced by a provider.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised poder preventivo granted in Spain, certified copy of the director's NIE (foreigner identity number), passport, bank-approved mandate sheet, registered-office lease or domiciliation agreement, and evidence of the director's social security / corporate immigration status if applicable; the bank will also ask for the UBO's professional biography.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Refusal or ambiguity in identifying ultimate beneficial owners, or any PEP/nominee suspicion regarding the SL's ownership chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full share-registry extract, formation chart identifying every natural person owning over 25%, declarations of no nominees signed by each shareholder, Titular Real declarations from the Spanish register, negative PEP screening from the bank's system, and, where appropriate, an independent AML compliance opinion by a Spanish abogado.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Preferred compliant route: notarised capital increase (ampliación de capital) or shareholder loan (préstamo socios) executed before a Spanish notary, registered at the Registro Mercantil, and reported to the Banco de España under the Foreign Investment Declaration regime. Wire instruction protocol requires SWIFT MT103 to the SL's euro IBAN, using the Remittance Information to cite the deed number, notary, registration date, and purpose code correlating to 'Foreign direct investment – equity participation' (BPM6 concept 1010/1080) or, for the loan, 'Inter-company financing operations'. The Bank of Spain threshold for mandatory investor filing is generally crossed where the non-resident investor holds 10% or more of share capital or where the investment value exceeds EUR 3,005,060.52; filings are due within one month. For the initial subscription the notary will route funds through a temporary escrow account (cuenta de capital) at a tier-1 bank (commonly CaixaBank or BBVA) and release to the operational treasury account after the inscription. For all inbound flows the bank will require a source-of-funds file: remitter bank statements, acquisition contract, and the declaration of foreign investment where applicable, ensuring the account beneficiary name and UETR match the executed corporate minutes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Payments to EU suppliers and ES counterparties run through SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001.001.09) or single SWIFT MT103 where immediate finality or a foreign currency is required; payments to non-EEA vendors (China, Mexico, Colombia, etc.) use SWIFT MT103 corporate-to-corporate wires with valid IBAN/SWIFT BIC, UETR, and strict compliance matching of beneficiary details. For project contractors in early trade phases, the recommended clearing rail is an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP 600), issued by the SL's issuing bank and advised/confirmed by a correspondent in the beneficiary's country, with MT700/MT707 flows; standby letters of credit (ISP98) and first-demand guarantees (URDG 758) are used as performance undertakings toward the grid operator. Short-term open-account flows can be supported by supply-chain finance, factoring, or forfaiting desks at Santander, BBVA, or CaixaBank, which also align with the Credit Line target payment rail. The SL shall maintain a EUR operating account, minor USD/CNH nostro balances for commodity hardware, and an inward LATAM collection sub-ledger to achieve natural treasury offsets before entering derivatives.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward (EUR/USD, EUR/CNH, EUR/MXN) under an ISDA 2002 / CSA master agreement, documented for genuine commercial hedge of the SCADA procurement and installation contract pipeline
FX swap (swap de divisas) to bridge temporary EUR/USD mismatches between the trade receivables collection and the vendor payment dates, with tenors up to twelve months

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on soft or non-convertible LATAM currencies (e.g., Argentine peso, Colombian peso, Venezuelan bolívar) permitted for hedge accounting of forecast local-currency revenue streams, with the notional settled in EUR

Cross-currency swap (CCS) available where the anchor bank syndicates a EUR/USD credit line or project finance facility tied to the SCADA infrastructure asset; not recommended before the first full operating year

Plain vanilla FX options and risk-reversal structures for hedging tender pipeline exposure to USD/MXN and USD/CLP, premium payable in EUR, subject to the bank's product governance and suitability assessment

Natural hedging via multi-currency operational accounts and local currency collection accounts in the target LATAM market, reducing the need for derivatives while preserving the corporate treasury's conservatism

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Accounts (Cuentas Anuales) including balance sheet, profit and loss statement, and memoria
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to 3,000 EUR per month of delay, administrative sanctions, and proceedings for dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if exceeding at least two of: net turnover > 7.5 million EUR, total assets > 3.75 million EUR, or average employees > 50
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual review and update of beneficial ownership details in Registro de Beneficiarios Finales; notification of shareholding transfers within 1 month

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (25% general rate per Art. 29.1 LIS Ley 27/2014; 15% preferential rate for newly created eligible entities on the first two taxable periods with a positive tax base)
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate for new SLs (Art. 29.1 LIS) for first two positive-base periods; 'capitalization reserve' 10% base reduction (Art. 25 LIS) lowering effective rate toward 22.5%; R&D&I tax credits (Art. 35 LIS) at 25-42% for qualifying automation/SCADA innovation; Digital/patent box (Art. 23 LIS) with 60% exemption on eligible IP income optionally applied
stage_6.tax_loss_carryforward_note: Spain allows indefinite carry-forward of negative tax bases (no statutory time limit) subject to quantitative caps: maximum offset 70% of taxable base for SMEs (INCN < €20M), 50% for INCN €20M-€60M, 25% for INCN ≥ €60M; the first €1M of annual offset is always allowable.
